title: Ranking All 20 Premier League Teams’ Performances on Matchday 10
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath6:30 PM ESTLiam Delap (middle) downed former club Manchester City with a brilliant brace of goals.  / Ritchie Sumpter/Nottingham Forest FC/Getty ImagesTen games down and if you thought you had the Premier League figured out this season, you might want to think again.

England’s top tier signed off for the November international break with the kind of topsy-turvy, accumulator-busting weekend of action that proves there is very rarely any point in making predictions.

Everton marked a landmark occasion for David Moyes with a win on Friday to kick off the weekend, while Chelsea and Manchester City’s hopes of serious title challenges took a further battering. Liverpool bounced back from last weekend’s defeat, Arsenal avoided being another surprise result (just) and Man Utd vs. Aston Villa offered up some industrial strength Barclays.

Another error-strewn performance from City. / Nigel French/PA Images/Getty ImagesThe traveling Manchester City Defensive Error Extravanganza rolled into Nottingham this weekend, with Joško Gvardiol taking the lead and Elliot Anderson and Marc Guéhi in supporting roles.Three losses in a row is humiliating for Enzo Maresca, with patience wearing very thing among fans. In fairness, his team are playing like they have other things on their mind.

Remarkably, Chelsea have lost three in a row to Sunderland. /  Stu Forster/Getty ImagesAnother worrying defeat in which João Pedro was badly missed. None of Chelsea’s midfield or attack won a duel or a tackle in the opening 20 minutes, while the defense hardly fared much better.Levi Colwill’s substitution at half time felt like a mercy killing from Xabi Alonso after he gave away the penalty.

Igor Thiago’s red compounded a terrible day out for Brentford. / Adam Davy/PA Images/Getty ImagesNot a great way to celebrate your 200th Premier League match, Brentford were second best all over the park against Brighton and recorded not one single shot on target.Igor Thiago’s red card may have been relatively soft, but—as the cliché goes—he gave referee Michael Oliver a decision to make.

Mathys Tel suffered a “bad injury” in the defeat. / George Wood/Getty ImagesAfter three wins in a row, this was Bad Spurs once again, with Roberto De Zerbi unable to find a solution for his team’s toothlessness in attack.Tottenham dominated possession at Elland Road but took just seven shots and created just 0.72 xG.

Gary O'Neil was candid about his side’s shortcomings. / Richard Calver/Getty ImagesIt’ll be cold comfort to Gary O'Neil that this was yet another weekend in which Ipswich weren’t outclassed overall, but still ended up without a win (or even a draw). O’Neil bemoaned the silly errors that led to both goals, putting it bluntly: “If you give the ball to the opposition number nine twice, then it’s going to be difficult. So that was basically the story of the game, really.”

Frank Lampard’s side threw away their lead. / Mark Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesWasteful and not for the first time this season, Frank Lampard’s side were undone in a second-half flurry, despite matching Everton for most of the evening.Lampard was, justifiably, left rueing two un-awarded penalty appeals including one for James Tarkowski tugging on Caleb Yirenkyi’s hair.“They’re saying it's not enough of a pull and I think it’s a hard area to be in. What is a hair pull?” The manager asked existentially.

Yéremy Pino was a bright spark for Palace / Jacques Feeney/Offside/Offside/Getty Images)Crystal Palace were pretty serviceable for large sections against Liverpool, with Yéremy Pino a busy, bar-clanking presence in attack. The Eagles had more possession (54%) and only one shot fewer than their opponents (19), but once the goals went in, Pierre Sage’s team— devoid of confidence—fell to pieces. This feels like the end of the line for the increasingly hangdog-looking Frenchman.

Unai Emery was probably the only man at Old Trafford to turn his back on the action ahead of the final whistle, heading down the tunnel two minutes before the end after Patrick Dorgu’s ultra-dramatic equalizer was allowed to stand.On one hand, scoring four times and getting a point away at Manchester United isn’t a terrible thing, but, on the other (much bigger) hand, throwing away a two-goal lead with only stoppage to go against this Manchester United is.

Rodrigo Muniz scored his first of the season. / Mike Hewitt/Getty ImagesA draw at Craven Cottage felt like a fair result for two teams still unsure of who they are and what they are doing.The action was condensed into the final ten minutes with the goals from Jacob Murphy and Rodrigo Muniz followed up by very smart saves from Bernd Leno and Lukás Hornícek.
A belter from Jacob Murphy at Craven Cottage 💥 pic.twitter.com/QHpJ0yQxWm

See above, but marginally better for Newcastle because it was away from home. Matthias Jaissle called it “a step in the right direction,” in the kind of post-match interview befitting of a match this forgettable.
Popping up with a vital equaliser when it mattered 👊🤳 #ShotOnSnapdragon pic.twitter.com/vRkwbU36dB

In the immortal words of Sir Alex Ferguson: football, bloody hell.It’s hard to rationally assess United’s bonkers comeback at Old Trafford, which was simultaneously brilliant and terrible. So, perhaps it’s better to just stuck it mid-table and move on.

Hull battled gamely but left with nothing. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesHull were not expected to get anything away at the champions ... And they didn’t. But, for a while, it looked like they just might.Konstantinos Tzolakis made nine saves, Elliot Stroud looked lively on the counter and the Tigers offered more evidence that they can mix it at this level.
WE KEEP GOING ✊ pic.twitter.com/cuiapuQjnk

Technically a win, yes, but not much to cheer on a frustrating, bore-fest at the Emirates, with captain Martin Ødegaard poking home in the second half to save some Gunners’ blushes.“We need to be much more chaotic,” Mikel Arteta surmised post-match.
Watch out, Gareth! 😅Thierno is soaring up the list of highest-scoring @premierleague Barrys! 📈 pic.twitter.com/Z7lq2TW6LM
